_about: Synthetic, hand-written labeled cases for the 16_decision_models study. NOT real CVEs. 'type' uses utils.models.VulnerabilityType enum values; 'severity' uses utils.models.SeverityLevel values; 'remote_exploit' is a yes/no boolean. Used to measure calibration and routing offline.

cases.text: Unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted packet that runs arbitrary code on the server.
A login form concatenates user input into a SQL query, letting an attacker dump the users table.
A comment field reflects user HTML without escaping, so a script runs in other visitors' browsers.
The password reset endpoint accepts any token, allowing full account takeover remotely.
A state-changing action lacks an anti-forgery token, so a malicious page can trigger it.
A stack buffer overflow in a local file parser corrupts memory when opening a crafted file.
Session tokens are generated with a predictable PRNG, so an attacker can guess valid sessions.
A verbose error page leaks the full stack trace and framework version to any visitor.
A deserialization endpoint instantiates arbitrary classes from untrusted input, giving remote code execution.
A search box passes raw input into a database query; blind boolean injection reveals row data.
A profile name field stores a script tag that fires for admins viewing the user list (stored XSS).
An admin API trusts a client-set role header, so a normal user can act as administrator.
A bank transfer form can be submitted cross-site because it only checks the session cookie.
A use-after-free in the local image decoder can crash the client or corrupt memory.
TLS is configured to accept an export-grade cipher, enabling an on-path downgrade attack.
A debug flag left on exposes an unauthenticated metrics page with internal hostnames.
A template engine evaluates user input server-side, allowing remote command execution.
An ORDER BY parameter is interpolated into SQL, letting an attacker exfiltrate columns.
A markdown preview renders inline event handlers, running attacker JavaScript on view.
JWT signature verification is skipped when the alg header is 'none', bypassing auth.
An email-change form has no CSRF protection, letting a crafted page hijack the account.
An integer overflow in length handling leads to a heap write past the buffer when parsing input.
Passwords are stored with unsalted MD5, so a database leak reveals them to brute force.
A directory listing is enabled on the uploads folder, exposing other users' filenames.
A file-upload handler executes uploaded PHP, giving an attacker a remote web shell.
A UNION-based injection in the product filter returns admin password hashes.
A URL parameter is echoed into the page unencoded, enabling reflected XSS via a link.
A hardcoded support account with a default password allows anyone to log in remotely.
A logout link performs a GET with no token, so a page can forcibly log victims out.
A format-string flaw in a local logging utility can be abused to read process memory.
An API encrypts cookies in ECB mode, so identical blocks leak structure to an eavesdropper.
A backup archive is served without auth at a predictable path, exposing config secrets.
